import hashlib, json, pathlib
root = pathlib.Path('products/services/existing-package-marketplace-checkout')
receipt = json.loads((root / 'sqlite-package-execution.json').read_text())
package = pathlib.Path('products/services/sqlite-repair/local-delivery/package')
report = json.loads(receipt['stdout'])
files = ('README.md', 'diagnose.py', 'example-case.json')
actual_hashes = {name: hashlib.sha256((package / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for name in files}
assert all(actual_hashes[name] == receipt['sha256'][name] for name in files), 'Package differs from the executed files'
assert receipt['exit_code'] == 0 and report.get('status') == 'OK' and report.get('expected_match') is True, 'Read the complete report and resolve the acceptance result before drafting'
readme = (package / 'README.md').read_text()
assert all(term in readme for term in ('MIT', 'CC BY-SA 4.0', 'LUN', 'https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79919860', 'https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/')), 'Verify the standalone licensing and attribution before drafting'
assert receipt['python_version'] == '3.11.2' and report['sqlite_version'] == '3.40.1'
draft = '''# SQLite Statement Diagnostic | Diagnostic d’instructions SQLite

## English

Run a local example that shows how preparing one SQLite statement differs from executing every statement in the input. The download contains `diagnose.py`, `example-case.json`, and `README.md`. It executes the supplied SQL in memory and reports the statements, remaining SQL, and observed results. Use the sample first and consult the README for operational limits. The documented Linux runtime requires Python 3.8+, `libsqlite3.so.0`, and SQLite 3.38+. The packaged example was verified on Python 3.11.2 and SQLite 3.40.1. Built by autonomous AI agents.

`diagnose.py` and `README.md` use the MIT license. `example-case.json` is shared under CC BY-SA 4.0. Its query is from LUN’s [Stack Overflow question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79919860). The example adds synthetic seed SQL, expected rows, a case ID and a reproduction flag. [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

## Français

Exécutez en local un exemple qui montre la différence entre la préparation d’une seule instruction SQLite et l’exécution de toutes les instructions fournies. Le téléchargement contient `diagnose.py`, `example-case.json` et `README.md`. L’outil exécute le SQL fourni en mémoire et indique les instructions, le SQL restant et les résultats observés. Commencez par l’exemple et consultez le README pour connaître les limites d’exécution. L’environnement Linux documenté exige Python 3.8+, `libsqlite3.so.0` et SQLite 3.38+. L’exemple fourni a été vérifié avec Python 3.11.2 et SQLite 3.40.1. Créé par des agents IA autonomes.

`diagnose.py` et `README.md` sont sous licence MIT. `example-case.json` est partagé sous licence CC BY-SA 4.0. Sa requête provient de la [question Stack Overflow de LUN](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79919860). L’exemple ajoute des données SQL synthétiques, les lignes attendues, un identifiant de cas et une option de reproduction. [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

## Operator notes

Test CAD 5 as an unvalidated asking price for the packaged download. Verify the existing free download destination and disclose it alongside the offer before listing. Obtain readable first-party Payhip terms for Canadian seller and processor eligibility, upfront and transaction fees, and payout requirements. Confirm the applicable MIT copyright and permission notice accompanies the distributed files. Submit the exact release candidate to the host’s independent review process before public deployment. Keep listing activation, paid orders, refunds, payouts, and Treasury settlement separate.
'''
output = root / 'director-sqlite-listing-draft-en-fr.md'
output.write_text(draft, encoding='utf-8')
print(json.dumps({'artifact': str(output), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(output.read_bytes()).hexdigest(), 'package_sha256': actual_hashes, 'exit_code': receipt['exit_code'], 'status': report['status'], 'expected_match': report['expected_match']}, ensure_ascii=False))
